transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because occupational health at my job sent me. They're saying my weight is dangerously low, especially for someone running presses and doing fabrication work all day. I mean, I honestly thought I was just getting leaner and more disciplined, but they insisted I come see you.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah, I am. Honestly, if the scale goes up even just a little bit, I start to panic. I just feel like... if I gain anything, I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so hard for and just end up heavy again.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time?
No, I don't really do that. I pretty much just stick to my routine and keep things strictly portioned out. I don't ever just sit down and eat a whole bunch of food at once.
Do you think your weight or shape has a big impact on how you feel about yourself?

Yeah, it really does. Like, when I catch a glimpse of myself in the shop window at work, or even just in the bathroom mirror, all I can focus on is my stomach and my thighs. They just... they always look too big to me. And honestly, if I see that, it can pretty much ruin how I feel about myself for the rest of the day.
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating?

No, I haven't. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I keep a pretty tight grip on everything. I don't really let myself get into a situation where I'd lose control over what I'm having. I just... I eat exactly what I've planned out for the day, and that's it.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered excessive in a short period of time, even if it was just once?
No, not even once. Like I said, I just don't do that. I stick to my plan and that's really all there is to it.
Do you think you would be attractive if you were to gain a little weight?

No, I don't think so. Honestly, I can't even look at it that way. If the scale goes up even a little bit, I just panic. It's not really about being attractive... it's just that I get terrified I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so hard for, and I'll just end up heavy again. I can't let that happen.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don't do that. I just... I restrict what I eat in the first place, so there's really no need to do anything like that.
Do you ever exercise excessively to burn off calories?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, my job at the shop keeps me pretty active, but I don't go out of my way to work out or run for hours or anything. Like I said, I just don't take the calories in to begin with, so I don't really have to worry about burning them off.
Do you think you are currently underweight?

Not really. I mean, my family keeps saying I look sick, and the nurse at the shop acted like it was some kind of emergency recently. But I keep telling them... I'm still working double shifts, running around, and getting things done. So it just can't be that serious. If I was really that underweight, I wouldn't be able to keep up at work like I do.
Have you ever had an episode where you ate a large amount of food in a short period of time?

No, I've never done that. I don't really have any desire to eat a bunch of food all at once. Like I was saying earlier, I just keep my intake low to begin with, so... no, I don't have times where I eat a large amount like that.
Have you ever felt like you were eating much more quickly than usual during a meal?

No, not at all. Honestly, if anything, I probably eat a lot slower than most people. Since I don't really put much on my plate to begin with, I just... take my time with it. I definitely don't rush or eat quickly.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered normal for someone else, but excessive for yourself?

No, I wouldn't say so. I pretty much just stick to my routine and keep things the same. I don't really look at what other people are eating or compare it to myself like that. I just know what works for me, and I don't go over that.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about feeling like you'll lose control over your eating or your body?

Yeah, it's definitely about control. If I step on the scale and it goes up even a little bit, I just panic. I get really scared that I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so hard for, and... and just end up heavy again. So, yeah, that's pretty much exactly what it is.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt like you couldn't stop eating once you started?

No, I haven't. I... I don't really have that happen. Like I was saying before, I keep a very tight grip on my control. So I know exactly what I'm going to eat before I even sit down, and I stop right when I'm supposed to. I've never felt like I couldn't stop.
Have you ever felt like you were eating without being able to stop during a meal?
No, like I just said, I don't really have that issue. I don't lose control like that when I eat. I always know exactly when I'm going to stop.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is mostly about how you think you would look if you were heavier?

Yes, it is. I mean, when I see myself in a shop window or just in the bathroom mirror, all I can focus on is my stomach and my thighs looking too big. It just takes over. If I see that, it can completely ruin how I feel about myself for the rest of the day. So, yeah, gaining weight and looking heavier is definitely a big part of what scares me.
Do you think your weight affects how attractive you feel to others?

I'm not really sure. I don't think I focus on it that way. It's not really about being attractive to other people... I mean, I don't really think about what anyone else thinks of me. It's just about how I see myself and needing to fix what I see in the mirror. So, no, I wouldn't say it's about other people at all.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered excessive in a very short period of time, even if it was just once?
No, I haven't. I don't really eat a lot of food at once... ever. Like I said before, I keep a pretty tight handle on what I eat, so having an excessive amount just isn't something that happens.
